evidence.claim: General Prayut Chan-o-cha is listed as the 29th Prime Minister, with Term 2 running from 2019-07-09 to 2023-09-04.
evidence.title: Cabinet Directory
evidence.excerpt: General Prayut Chan-o-cha is listed as the 29th Prime Minister, with Term 2 running from 2019-07-09 to 2023-09-04.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government roster with tenure dates.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 period and anchors office identity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct office record for Prayut Chan-o-cha.
contrary_evidence: Office identity alone does not show any nuclear or existential-risk decision-making.

evidence.claim: Thailand's House passed the first reading of a 3.185-trillion-baht draft budget for fiscal 2023, and Prayut said the budget would boost Covid recovery, sustain development, reduce inequality, and distribute aid transparently.
evidence.title: House passes first reading of THB3tn budget bill
evidence.excerpt: Thailand's House passed the first reading of a 3.185-trillion-baht draft budget for fiscal 2023, and Prayut said the budget would boost Covid recovery, sustain development, reduce inequality, and distribute aid transparently.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous parliamentary reporting with specific budget figures and the prime minister's own stated purpose for the bill.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 budget-setting evidence within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Prayut as prime minister presenting and defending the budget.
contrary_evidence: A proposed budget is not the same as successful implementation.
Opposition votes and parliamentary friction show the policy was contested.

evidence.claim: The FY2022 budget brief says the annual budget is a plan for disbursing state funds and managing monetary and fiscal policy, and that budget policy prioritizes integrated allocation, cutting low-priority projects, reducing social inequality, stimulating economic expansion, public participation, and vulnerable groups.
evidence.title: THAILAND’S BUDGET IN BRIEF FISCAL YEAR 2022
evidence.excerpt: The FY2022 budget brief says the annual budget is a plan for disbursing state funds and managing monetary and fiscal policy, and that budget policy prioritizes integrated allocation, cutting low-priority projects, reducing social inequality, stimulating economic expansion, public participation, and vulnerable groups.
evidence.source_locator: pp. 230-259; especially lines 230-257 and 270-280 in the text version
evidence.source_confidence_reason: It is a mirrored copy of the official Budget Bureau brief and the text is internally consistent and detailed, but the host is not the originating publisher.
evidence.period_fit: Direct FY2022 program document within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level budget policy under Prayut's government; strong attribution to his administration, weaker for his personal authorship.
contrary_evidence: The document is a plan, not proof of implementation or outcome.
External shocks still shaped FY2022 execution.

evidence.claim: Prayuth survived a no-confidence vote with 256 votes in favor and 206 against, after four days of public grilling over corruption and economic mismanagement.
evidence.title: Thai PM Survives 4th No-Confidence Vote in Parliament
evidence.excerpt: Prayuth survived a no-confidence vote with 256 votes in favor and 206 against, after four days of public grilling over corruption and economic mismanagement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting republished by VOA with precise vote totals and context on the coalition's parliamentary strength.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and squarely within the ruler-period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Prayut's coalition management and parliamentary control, though not proof of policy success.
contrary_evidence: The opposition framed the vote as about corruption and economic mismanagement.
Survival in parliament does not by itself show effective governance.

evidence.claim: The PPRP-led coalition failed to make quorum, adjourning the House for the 17th time, and the article describes the coalition as fragile and internally disunited.
evidence.title: Opposition ups pressure on Prayut as coalition misses House quorum again
evidence.excerpt: The PPRP-led coalition failed to make quorum, adjourning the House for the 17th time, and the article describes the coalition as fragile and internally disunited.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local reporting with concrete parliamentary detail; less authoritative than Reuters but still specific and time-locked.
evidence.period_fit: Within the target year and directly about coalition functionality.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Prayut's governing coalition and his ability to keep legislators aligned, though factional autonomy matters.
contrary_evidence: Attendance failure may reflect MPs' behavior rather than direct personal action by Prayut.
The article also notes the coalition and opposition both share responsibility for House dysfunction.

evidence.claim: Prayuth and 10 ministers survived the censure motion, with 256 votes of confidence against 206 no-confidence votes, and the article says the coalition remained intact after the vote.
evidence.title: Prayuth, all other censured ministers survive no-confidence vote
evidence.excerpt: Prayuth and 10 ministers survived the censure motion, with 256 votes of confidence against 206 no-confidence votes, and the article says the coalition remained intact after the vote.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and vote tally section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: It reports a specific parliamentary result, but is a secondary local outlet with less authority than Reuters.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and directly relevant to coalition control.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Prayut's coalition discipline and parliamentary bargaining, with major influence from coalition partners.
contrary_evidence: The article explicitly says the vote was widely expected to be followed by a cabinet reshuffle or more bargaining.
Survival does not show strong execution in policy delivery.

evidence.claim: The page lists FY2022 quarterly performance and budget-spending reports (S งป.301/302), annual ministry performance reports, and the government performance report for Gen. Prayut's first year, showing an active monitoring and reporting framework for implementation.
evidence.title: Office of Permanent Secretary policy_plan page
evidence.publisher: Office of Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Public Health
evidence.excerpt: The page lists FY2022 quarterly performance and budget-spending reports (S งป.301/302), annual ministry performance reports, and the government performance report for Gen. Prayut's first year, showing an active monitoring and reporting framework for implementation.
evidence.source_locator: Year 2565 section of the policy-plan page
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry portal with explicit document list for FY2022 reporting and performance tracking.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Prayut's cabinet and the Public Health ministry; this supports implementation machinery rather than Prayut's personal authorship.
contrary_evidence: This is a reporting framework and document index, not a consolidated audit of delivery quality.
It does not by itself prove that implementation met targets.

evidence.claim: The 2022 annual report says it summarizes major education results under the ministry's action plan, including national-security education, research and development, lifelong human development, disadvantaged persons, disabled people, elderly people, teacher capacity, environmental stewardship, and public administration.
evidence.title: รายงานประจำปี 2565 กระทรวงศึกษาธิการ
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 annual report says it summarizes major education results under the ministry's action plan, including national-security education, research and development, lifelong human development, disadvantaged persons, disabled people, elderly people, teacher capacity, environmental stewardship, and public administration.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry page describing its 2022 annual report and the scope of implementation covered in it.
evidence.period_fit: Covers FY2022 implementation, published shortly after the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mixed attribution to Prayut's cabinet and the education ministry; this is stronger on implementation than on Prayut personally.
contrary_evidence: This is still a ministry summary, not a line-by-line execution audit.
The page does not isolate Prayut's unique contribution from broader bureaucratic execution.

evidence.claim: The IMF says Thailand's authorities had started to withdraw large pandemic-related support in FY2022, reducing fiscal stimulus by 1.2 percent of GDP versus FY2021, extending some energy-price measures through the fiscal year, and approving targeted cash transfers to vulnerable groups worth about 0.2 percent of GDP.
evidence.title: Thailand: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Thailand
evidence.excerpt: The IMF says Thailand's authorities had started to withdraw large pandemic-related support in FY2022, reducing fiscal stimulus by 1.2 percent of GDP versus FY2021, extending some energy-price measures through the fiscal year, and approving targeted cash transfers to vulnerable groups worth about 0.2 percent of GDP.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF staff report with concrete fiscal-policy detail and a clear link to 2022 policy decisions.
evidence.period_fit: Directly addresses FY2022 policy adaptation within the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Thai authorities under Prayut's government; not all of the policy choice is uniquely personal to Prayut, but the cabinet clearly owned the response.
contrary_evidence: The report is partly forward-looking and advisory.
The IMF also notes that energy subsidies were still costly and regressive.

evidence.claim: Thailand's cabinet extended energy-price support and tourism measures, including a 100-baht monthly cooking-gas subsidy for low-income earners, freezing vehicle gas prices for taxi drivers, and seeking refinery contributions to the oil fund; Prayut said fiscal discipline meant spending had to be sparse.
evidence.title: Thailand extends measures to tackle high oil prices, help tourism
evidence.excerpt: Thailand's cabinet extended energy-price support and tourism measures, including a 100-baht monthly cooking-gas subsidy for low-income earners, freezing vehicle gas prices for taxi drivers, and seeking refinery contributions to the oil fund; Prayut said fiscal discipline meant spending had to be sparse.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters dateline paragraphs in the article body
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters contemporaneous reporting with specific cabinet actions and an exact date.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and responsive to an inflation shock.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet action under Prayut; attribution is strong for the policy choice, weaker for any downstream effectiveness claim.
contrary_evidence: Temporary relief does not show long-term success.
The policy was a defensive response to external energy shocks rather than a structural reform.

evidence.claim: Finance Minister Arkhom Termpittayapaisith said Thailand's stimulus would become more targeted toward vulnerable groups and low-income households as more people returned to work.
evidence.title: Thai government spending to target low-income groups - Finance Minister
evidence.excerpt: Finance Minister Arkhom Termpittayapaisith said Thailand's stimulus would become more targeted toward vulnerable groups and low-income households as more people returned to work.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting of an explicit policy shift by the finance minister, contemporaneous and specific.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to the government's policy adjustment path.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Prayut's finance and economic team; this is good evidence of course correction, though not uniquely Prayut's personal action.
contrary_evidence: The statement is a policy direction, not an implementation audit.
It does not prove the new targeting fully displaced broader support.

unresolved_gaps: No Prayut-specific 2022 nuclear or other existential-risk choice is evidenced; the package is mostly inherited treaty and safeguards context.
No direct cabinet-minute or NSC record ties Prayut personally to each 2022 Ukraine or Myanmar diplomatic position.
Direct command-chain evidence for specific police operations, protest policing, and protest-prosecution decisions is limited.
Direct documentary proof of Prayut's personal authorization of spyware or surveillance is absent.
Ruler-level evidence on appointments quality and 2022 rule-setting for competition, property rights, and investment remains thin.
Outcome evidence is stronger than direct ruler attribution across health, education, and social protection.
No direct 2022 evidence of hidden assets, family profit, or proven deception beyond disclosure opacity and allegations.
There is no single consolidated FY2022 execution audit tying the program, implementation, and outcomes back to Prayut's full cabinet-level agenda.
